key: A senior batsman in a Ranji side has had
name: ch28_coach_nets_reputation
alt: At the cricket nets, a coach sits beside a slumping senior batsman, pointing at a tablet of match footage and reminding him the young players look up to him; the batsman, bat on his knee, starts to sit up straighter.
scene: A wide view of cricket practice nets at a state ground in late afternoon, green netting stretched on poles on the right, a worn pitch strip and a few red balls lying on the grass. In the centre foreground, a wooden bench. On it sits a senior batsman (mid 30s, white cricket kit, pads still strapped on, cap pushed back), his bat resting across his knees, shoulders slumped a little but face turning up with a hint of resolve. Beside him sits the coach (50s, grey tracksuit, whistle on a cord, short grey hair), leaning in warmly, one hand on the batsman's shoulder and the other holding up a tablet showing a small batting figure on screen. Above the coach, a speech bubble with three small figures of young players and a star, to show 'the young lads watch you'. On the left in the background, two young players in whites stand at the nets watching the senior man with admiration. Behind the bench, a small chalkboard scoreboard lists three low scores "12" "8" "15" with a downward arrow, the slump everyone can see. A thin curved arrow runs from the coach's bubble to the batsman's straightening back, showing the good name lifting him. Warm golden light, encouraging mood rather than scolding. Label: "LIVE UP TO IT" across the top centre of the picture.

key: A grandmother hands her teenage grandson
name: ch28_grandmother_rangoli_steady_hand
alt: On Diwali evening a grandmother tells the neighbours her grandson has the steadiest hand in the family, while he kneels carefully perfecting the curves of a rangoli in front of the house.
scene: A front view of the doorstep of a small Indian house on Diwali evening, the wall off-white with a wooden door, a string of marigolds over it and small clay diyas glowing along the step. In the centre foreground, a teenage boy (about 15, blue kurta, sleeves pushed up) kneels on the ground, carefully drawing a large round rangoli in coral, amber, teal and plum powder; his tongue is between his teeth in concentration, one hand pinching colour, a small rubbed-out wobbly curve beside the pattern shows he is redoing the lines. On the left, the grandmother (late 60s, cream cotton sari with a maroon border, spectacles, grey bun) stands proudly with one hand gesturing toward him, talking to two neighbours, a middle-aged woman in a green sari and a man in a white kurta, who nod impressed. A speech bubble from the grandmother shows a simple hand icon with a gold star, meaning 'the steadiest hand'. On the right edge, a small inset shows the one earlier decent rangoli he once made, a simpler flower, with a green tick, the real ability behind the praise. A dotted arrow runs from her bubble to the boy's careful hand. Warm lamplight, festive and proud. Label: "STEADIEST HAND" at the top above the grandmother's bubble.

key: The quiet office boy in a Chennai firm
name: ch28_office_boy_eye_for_detail
alt: In a Chennai office a senior manager signing a courier slip praises the office boy's neat handwriting; on the right, a year later, the same young man sits at a desk with ledgers, training as a junior accountant.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same young man (about 20, slim, neat side parting) in both halves. LEFT panel: a modest Chennai office with a steel cupboard, a ceiling fan and a window with coconut palms outside. The young man wears a plain grey shirt and holds a steel tray with two small glasses of tea in one hand and a stack of files under his arm. A senior manager (50s, white shirt, spectacles, moustache) sits at a desk signing a small courier slip, looking up with a pleased expression and pointing at the slip, where neat handwriting is visible. A speech bubble from the manager shows a magnifying glass over a neat line of writing with a star. The young man looks surprised and quietly proud. RIGHT panel, one year later: the same young man, now in a light blue shirt with a pen in his pocket, sits at his own small desk with an open ledger, a calculator and a stack of account files, while an older clerk (grey hair, spectacles) leans over his shoulder, pointing at a column and teaching him. A small wall calendar reads "1 YEAR LATER". A long arrow sweeps from the left panel's star to the right panel's ledger. Soft daylight, hopeful mood. Labels: "CHAI BOY" at the top of the left panel, "JUNIOR ACCOUNTANT" at the top of the right panel.

key: Your father has refused, firmly, to let
name: ch28_father_second_look
alt: At night a young man sits with his father at the dining table, offering him the job offer papers again and reminding him he is the one who listens to facts; the father, glasses on, leans in to take a second look.
scene: An interior view of a middle-class Indian home at night, a dining table under a single warm hanging lamp, a steel water jug and two glasses on the table, a window behind showing a dark blue sky with a crescent moon, the room itself still light and calm. On the right, the father (late 50s, white vest under an open checked shirt, grey moustache, reading glasses pushed up on his forehead) sits with arms folded at first, but his body is leaning slightly forward with curiosity. On the left, his son (mid 20s, t-shirt, respectful posture) sits across, sliding a small stack of papers toward him: the top sheet shows a simple drawing of a building and a shield icon for the hostel and safety rules. A speech bubble from the son contains a simple icon of a balance scale with a magnifying glass, meaning 'you listen to the facts'. In the background doorway, the sister (early 20s, salwar kameez, dupatta) stands peeking in, hands clasped, hopeful. A dotted arrow runs from the papers toward the father's hand, which is just lowering his glasses to read. A small hourglass beside the father shows nothing is decided yet, only a fair listen. Quiet, warm, respectful mood. Label: "A SECOND LOOK" at the top centre.

key: watchman lets delivery boys wander in
name: ch28_watchman_safest_gate
alt: At a housing society gate the secretary kindly tells the watchman people say theirs is the safest gate thanks to him and offers a clipboard; next to the cabin, a delivery rider signs the register.
scene: A wide street-level view of the main gate of an Indian housing society: a painted iron gate on the left, a small blue watchman's cabin in the centre with a window and a stool, apartment blocks with balconies and potted plants in the background. In front of the cabin stands the watchman (about 50, khaki uniform shirt, cap, thick moustache), standing taller with a surprised, proud smile, one hand on his chest. Facing him, the society secretary (40s, woman in a teal salwar kameez, spectacles, phone in hand) speaks warmly and holds out a new brown clipboard with a pen clipped to it. Her speech bubble shows a gate with a shield and a green tick, meaning 'the safest gate'. On the right, a delivery rider (20s, red t-shirt, helmet in hand, a cardboard parcel under his arm) leans on a small ledge at the cabin window and signs a big open register book, the pages filled with neat rows of entries. A faded phone in the secretary's other hand shows an unsent angry message with a red cross over it, the notice she chose not to post. A small inset at top right shows the register a week later, every line filled, with a green tick. Bright morning light, friendly mood. Label: "SAFEST GATE" above the cabin roof.

key: A new class teacher in a Pune school
name: ch28_backbencher_class_monitor
alt: A new teacher in a Pune classroom makes the backbench gang leader the class monitor with a badge; he now turns around and shushes his noisy friends in the back row during announcements.
scene: A classroom in a Pune school seen from the side front, wooden benches in rows, a green chalkboard on the left wall, a ceiling fan and a window with bright daylight. On the left at the front, the new class teacher (early 30s, woman in a mustard cotton sari, hair in a neat bun, holding a register) stands smiling confidently, gesturing toward one boy. In the centre, the former backbench gang leader (about 14, school uniform of white shirt and navy shorts, tie loose, spiky hair) stands by his bench at the back, wearing a shiny round monitor badge pinned on his chest, and turns toward the back row holding a finger to his lips, shushing them, looking serious and responsible. In the back row on the right, three of his friends (boys of the same age in uniform, one with a paper plane, one mid-laugh) freeze and quieten down, wide-eyed. On the chalkboard, the only writing is "SPORTS PERIOD" with a simple cricket bat drawing. A speech bubble from the teacher shows the whole class as small dots following one larger dot with a star. A curved arrow runs from the badge to the quietened back row, showing the new name turning his pull toward order. Cheerful daylight mood. Label: "MONITOR" just above the boy's badge.
